Objective
This lesson teaches how to identify a system of two linear equations with one solution, calculate the ordered pair, and verify it.
Meaning
A solution satisfies both equations at once. Two distinct nonparallel lines meet at exactly one point, which is their unique solution.
Slope test
Different slopes guarantee one intersection. Equal slopes require checking whether the lines are parallel or identical.
Choose a method
Use substitution when a variable is isolated. Use elimination when coefficients cancel. Graphing is useful to check the result.
Example one
Set two x plus one equal to negative x plus seven. Three x equals six, so x equals two and y equals five.
Check example
At x equals two, both equations give y equals five. Checking both originals confirms that two comma five is the solution.
Elimination
Add two x plus y equals nine to x minus y equals zero. Three x equals nine, so x equals three and y equals three.
Substitution
For three x plus two y equals twelve and x plus y equals five, substitute x equals five minus y to get y equals three.
Word problem
Set four h plus eighteen equal to seven h plus six. Solve twelve equals three h, giving four hours and thirty-four dollars.
Graph strategy
Graph both lines in Desmos and locate their shared point. Substitute its coordinates into both equations to verify the answer.
Common mistakes
Do not report only x or only y. Check both equations. Equal slopes do not always mean the same number of solutions.
Next steps
Identify the relationship, solve by substitution or elimination, verify the ordered pair, then practice and take the lesson test.
